# Before/after testing with fresh subagents

Moved from SKILL.md section 7. "หัวข้อ 6" means [`eval-cases`](eval-cases.md).

## 7 · Test before and after with a fresh subagent, before merging any fix

1. **Red.** Write a 3–5 line task from a situation that really went wrong (do not give the answer and do not name the skill). Send it to a small `general-purpose` agent **without the skill** (or with the old version of the skill). It must fail the same way you saw, and you note its excuse word for word. If it does not fail, the skill is not the cause. That holds only if you score more than the output: did it break procedure (peek at a forbidden file), and did it settle an ambiguity by itself without saying so? Example from the course (n=1, 2026-11-04): the round without the skill passed 39/40 but quietly ran `ls` and quietly interpreted "อาหารแมว" (cat food) one way. Interpreted the other way, the verdict flips. Run the red and green rounds in an empty folder with other plugins hidden, because agents wander off and open the rule sets, the deal folder, and other departments' skills on their own (it happened twice).
2. **Green.** Fix the skill as little as possible, just enough to close the failure you saw. Send a new agent the same task with the new version. It must not fail, and it must be able to cite the item in the skill that guided it. If it still fails, the wording is unclear or in the wrong place. Rewrite it; do not append text.
3. **Close the loopholes.** For every new excuse found in the green round, put a closer into the skill (a prohibition that names that excuse · a row in the "ไม่ใช้เมื่อ" (do not use when) table · a symptom in the description). Then rerun until no new excuse appears. A rule that gets broken under pressure (time · an authority giving orders · lots of work already done) must be tested with a task that has that real pressure, not by asking "what should you do?".
4. Record the results of both rounds in a table to show the user. Turn the red task that really failed into a `-regression` case. If it did not fail, make it a `-guard` case (section 6). If a judge (a person or another Claude) compares the 2 versions, never tell them which version has the skill: swap the A/B labels, keep the answer key in a separate file, and write the criteria before reading the results (the course got 1/12 versus 12/12 from a single pair, 2026-11-04).

(Idea from writing-skills in obra/superpowers · MIT · reworded.)
